turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Well, I'm an event planner, and recently I've had to be a lot more visible at work—like, actually out in front of people. And... I just can't stop staring at this one part of my face in photos. It looks really uneven to me. I keep bringing it up, but everyone else says they barely see anything. It's just really bothering me, so I figured I should come in.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes an inability to stop staring at a perceived uneven part of their face in photos, which others say they barely see, indicating a preoccupation with a perceived flaw in appearance.

turns.doctor_question: About how much time each day do you find yourself thinking about or checking this part of your face?
turns.patient_response: Honestly, it takes up a good amount of my day. I don't track the exact hours, but... well, like before I send out event pictures or join a vendor meeting, I'll just keep checking my face in my phone camera. I end up retaking photos a bunch of times, or I have to make sure I tilt my head a certain way so it doesn't look as bad. Sometimes I'll even ask a coworker if I look weird. It just adds up, and it can eat up enough time that I actually fall behind on my planning stuff.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient describes repetitive behaviors such as repeatedly checking their face in a phone camera, retaking photos, and seeking reassurance from coworkers about their appearance.

turns.doctor_question: Deep down, do you feel there's a chance your perception might be exaggerated, or are you completely convinced that your face is visibly defective?
turns.patient_response:
I mean... I'm not really sure. When my friends or people at work tell me they don't see it, part of me thinks, okay, maybe it's not as bad as I think it is. They wouldn't all just lie to me. 

But then I look in the mirror or see a picture, and it's just right there. It looks so obvious and wrong to me. So I guess I don't know for sure... it just feels really real when I'm looking at it.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes seeing an obvious defect in their face that feels very real to them, while acknowledging that others say they cannot see it.

turns.doctor_question: Besides the concerns about your facial appearance, do you have any other repetitive, unwanted thoughts or habits you feel driven to perform, like checking things, washing, or needing things in a specific order?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I mean, I like to keep my event binders organized, but that's just part of the job. I don't have any weird habits like washing my hands over and over or checking the stove. It's really just... the thing with my face. That's the only thing that gets stuck in my head like that.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient reiterates that her concerns about her face are the only thoughts that get stuck in her head.
symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient denies having any other unwanted thoughts getting stuck in her head besides her facial appearance.
symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient explicitly denies having repetitive habits like washing hands repeatedly or checking the stove.
